back: A reduction in the amount owed for paying within a stated time. Recorded as discount allowed or received.
Cash discount given to customers: an expense.
Cash discount received from suppliers: income (added to gross profit).

front: Is trade discount recorded in the ledger?
back: No. It is deducted on the invoice; only the net amount is recorded.

front: Where is discount allowed entered in the three-column cash book?
back: In the discount column on the debit side, beside the receipt.

front: Where is discount received entered in the three-column cash book?
back: In the discount column on the credit side, beside the payment.
No. They are memorandum columns: totalled and posted (allowed to the debit of discount allowed; received to the credit of discount received).
Amount owed (after trade discount) × cash discount %. Amount paid = amount owed − cash discount.
Credit the customer's account with both the money received and the discount allowed.
